Subject: Post-call: Integration next steps & model routing

Hi Priya / Alex,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciate the deep-dive into Acme Health's search/triage workflow. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single place to reference: 

Recap (from our discovery):
- Primary use-case: patient support ticket triage + internal KB search + reranking for clinician triage.
- Expected peak QPS: ~120 requests/sec for embedding/rerank path, with 1–3k tokens for some follow-ups.
- Latency SLO: 300ms p90 for reranker path; 1–2s acceptable for longer generative follow-ups.
- Data constraints: PHI in payloads; must be VPC/private deployment or dedicated with KMS.

Open items we discussed that would help our integration plan:
1) Auth model: will you be able to support customer-managed mTLS or prefer API keys + OIDC?
2) SDK usage: do you want to embed our JS SDK in the frontend for low-latency calls, or route everything via a backend proxy?
3) Routing policies: priorities between latency vs cost (e.g., prefer low-cost quantized models unless p90 latency > X).
4) Embeddings & reranker: target recall/latency tradeoffs and acceptable tokenization/embedding sizes.

Next steps I propose:
- We’ll send a short integration checklist and an architecture diagram (attached).
- If you confirm auth preference (mTLS vs API key+OIDC), we’ll draft the config for routing policies and fallback chains.
- Schedule a 60-min tech session with Rishi (serving runtime) to walk infra + SLOs.

Attachments: redwood-integration-arch.png (high level), redwood-routing-examples.md (policy examples).

Are you available for the tech session on Wed or Thu afternoon PST?

Thanks,
Dev

Hi Dev,

Thanks for the recap — this is helpful. Quick answers and a few clarifying questions from our side: 

Auth: We prefer mTLS for production across VPC/private deployments for PHI. For POC, API keys are fine internally. Do you support customer-side cert rotation?

SDK vs proxy: We’d like to keep the frontend thin: embeddings and rerank calls should go through a backend proxy so we can audit payloads, while some real-time UI generation could use a frontend SDK. Do you have examples for hybrid setups?

Routing & fallback: We need the ability to set region routing (EU vs US) and latency-first policies for clinician-facing flows. Prefer fallback chains that try cheaper quantized models first, but can escalate to larger ones if confidence < threshold or latency budget allows. Can you show a sample policy DSL?

Embeddings/reranker: Our initial vector DB is Pinecone. We expect 2–4k vectors/day added initially; embedding dims ~1024. Reranker p90 target is 300ms. If reranker is slow, can we run a cheaper lexical fallback?

Finally, can you share a ballpark cost delta for enabling dedicated capacity vs hosted (for the reranker path)? We’ll need this for our procurement partners.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Rao
Head of Search & Knowledge, Acme Health

Hi Priya — great questions. Answers below + a concrete example for routing/policy that should map to your requirements. I’ve attached a short examples doc (redwood-routing-examples.md) and the high-level arch diagram.

Auth & cert rotation:
- Production (Private / Dedicated): we support customer-managed mTLS with automated cert rotation via our control plane; you can provide a CA or use our managed CA with rotation policies. We also support OIDC for user-level auth and API keys for service-level access.

SDK vs Proxy pattern:
- Hybrid pattern: frontend SDK for short-lived UI interactions (e.g., autocomplete), backend proxy for any request that contains PHI or requires audit logs. Our JS/TS SDKs include a lightweight client and recommended middleware for proxying. Example: frontend requests -> backend proxy (authn/audit) -> Redwood dedicated endpoint.

Routing / Policy DSL (high-level example):
- Policy: clinician-priority
  - match: route.tags contains 'clinician'
  - latency_budget_ms: 300
  - prefer_cost: false
  - fallback_chain: [gpt-quantized-2, gpt-pt-3-small, gpt-pt-3-large-hosted]
  - region_preference: ['us-west-2', 'us-east-1']
  - on_latency_exceed: escalate_to: gpt-pt-3-large-hosted

Notes: you can express cost vs latency as a weighted objective. The control plane exposes a JSON/YAML policy; the examples doc has a full snippet you can paste into the console.

Embeddings & reranker:
- Embedding dims 1024 is standard; Pinecone integration is tested. For reranking we recommend a two-stage pipeline: vector retrieval (100–500 candidates) -> fast lightweight reranker (quantized model) -> high-quality reranker for top 10 when confidence < thresh. This reduces average cost while keeping tail quality.
- Lexical fallback: yes — policy can include a precomputed lexical score and use that as a final fallback when reranker latency exceeds budget.

Capacity / cost guidance (ballpark):
- Hosted (on-demand): lower upfront, higher per-token cost; good for POC.
- Dedicated (reserved GPUs): ~40–60% lower per-token cost at steady usage for embedding/rerank heavy workloads with predictable QPS. I’ll include a capacity sketch (attached) and can run more precise modeling once you share expected RPS distribution and token lengths.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm auth preference for POC vs production (mTLS for prod).
2) If you’re good, we’ll schedule a 60-min tech session with Rishi to walk the routing DSL, dashboard, and A/B rollout options.
3) I’ll also share a draft SOW and cost delta for dedicated vs hosted.

Thanks — looping Rishi for the tech session scheduling: @rishi, any availability Wed afternoon PST?

Best,
Dev

Thanks — quick engineering note from my side after skimming the numbers:

Questions we need to size:
- QPS distribution (p95/p99 spikes) and expected concurrency. 120 QPS average might require 2–3 dedicated GPUs for reranker if running medium-sized models per request without batching.
- Typical sequence lengths for generate/feedback loops (if you have 3k tokens often, we’ll need to tune KV cache sizing).

Recommendations:
- Canary rollout: start with a small % of traffic to quantized model, monitor p90 latency and quality metrics (we can wire this into your evaluation set).
- Autoscaling + burst: configure dedicated pool with autoscale and a small hosted fallback for critical clinician flows (so you never drop below SLA).

I attached a quick capacity-estimate.xlsx with a back-of-envelope calc. Dev — happy to go through in the tech call and produce a more precise plan once Priya confirms authenticity/PKI preference.

-rishi
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
